properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency of the Ethereum toolchain (pulled via elliptic for HmacDRBG nonce generation in secp256k1 signing, and via ethereumjs-util). The shipped build includes these hash implementations whether or not each is invoked; SHA-2 family is quantum-adequate for most uses but below the CNSA 2.0 384-bit digest bar. Changeable here by dependency upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js ships MD5 as an available module in the shipped dependency graph (active via @truffle/contract-schema, which is a direct dependency). No MD5 call site in first-party code; the app's only live MD5 use is gravatar-api/blueimp-md5 (reported separately). Available in the shipped library, not invoked by the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 available in crypto-js@3.3.0 in the shipped graph via @truffle/contract-schema (direct dep @truffle/contract). No first-party SHA-1 call site; declaration-level presence in the shipped library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The signature primitive of the Ethereum account provisioned in truffle.js (hardcoded-mnemonic HD wallet, reported separately as the live use chain). Classical ECDSA is a deadline problem rather than a harvesting one: migrate on a schedule to ML-DSA; Ethereum's account abstraction roadmap is the migration vehicle. Changeable here only at the protocol level — the chain, not the app, fixes the signature scheme.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum Keccak-256 (pre-FIPS padding), used as the storage-key hash for the on-chain user database and config (userManager.sol:41-44, Setup.sol:21-24, utilities.sol:12,19-27, strings.sol:346 in first-party source). The build artifacts are compiled mirrors of that live source — I reported the source use site separately so the inventory points at the code a reader can change. Keccak-256 is quantum-safe (Grover gives only square-root preimage speedup). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES via crypto-js 3.3.0 (2015 vintage; the library also contains legacy MD5/SHA-1/DES/RC4 primitives) shipped through the Truffle contract toolchain; not invoked directly by application code. Changeable here via dependency upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP39 seed derivation is live at truffle.js:12 over a HARDCODED 12-word mnemonic (reported separately with hardcoded_material=[seed] and pbkdf_iterations=2048). The KDF itself is hash-based (quantum-adequate), but 2048 iterations is far below modern password-KDF guidance — it is the BIP39 standard, changeable only by switching away from BIP39 wallets. Changeable here as part of the wallet-provisioning redesign.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Memory-hard KDF used by ethereumjs-wallet@1.0.1 (direct dependency, used in truffle.js) and ethereumjs-util@7 for Ethereum V3 keystore encryption. The first-party code only uses hdkey.fromMasterSeed, so scrypt-js is shipped-and-available rather than invoked by the application; the keystore path exists if wallet export is ever used. Changeable here by dependency choice.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Provides the pure-JS SHA-256/SHA-1 implementations used by create-hash/create-hmac, which feed pbkdf2 and thus the live bip39.mnemonicToSeedSync call at truffle.js:12 — part of the active signing toolchain. Changeable here by dependency upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The ECDSA library behind Ethereum account signing in this project's toolchain; its secp256k1 keys sign every transaction the truffle.js wallet sends (the live key-derivation and signing chain is reported separately at truffle.js:16-17,29). Quantum-vulnerable signature primitive — migration to ML-DSA-class signatures is a protocol-level change.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-chain only: generates a throwaway self-signed X.509 cert for the local dev server when https is enabled; not part of the production bundle. Presence recorded because the build ships it and it decides dev-serve TLS posture. Changeable here by dev tooling choice.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hash toolkit in the shipped Ethereum toolchain: elliptic's HmacDRBG consumes it to generate secp256k1 signing nonces, and ethereumjs-util uses it in address/checksum helpers. Available in the shipped library; the SHA-2 members are quantum-adequate. Changeable here by dependency upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live call chain: truffle.js:12 bip39.mnemonicToSeedSync → pbkdf2 (HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations) → BIP32 master key → the secp256k1 account that signs Ropsten transactions. The seed derivation and its hardcoded input are reported separately as findings (hardcoded seed; ECDSA account key). Changeable here by redesigning wallet provisioning (env/KMS-sourced mnemonic).
